narrative:
The model estimated that you have a 63 percent chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. In this admissions process, that risk level was high enough to deny your law school application; it does not mean failure is certain.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank position. You were in the second decile, far below the accepted-student average of about the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward bar failure. Your undergraduate GPA was the next most important factor, but it actually pushed toward passing: at 3.10 it is only slightly below the accepted average of 3.23. The third factor, your first-year class rank, also pushed toward failure because your second-decile standing was well below the accepted average of about the sixth decile. Your gender and race were not used.

To strengthen a future application, focus on what you can change: speak with admissions or academic advising about provisional admission and bar-readiness support; take additional rigorous upper-level coursework or a post-baccalaureate program to raise your academic profile; consider retaking the LSAT if it can improve; and prepare a clear plan showing how you will address the academic patterns behind the prediction before reapplying.
